subject.en: United States-produced Iron and Steel in Public Works Projects
subject.es: United States-produced Iron and Steel in Public Works Projects
subject.ht: United States-produced Iron and Steel in Public Works Projects

note.en: Floor vote: third reading. The staff analysis says the bill helps contractors using American steel: “A private contractor that use iron or steel products that are produced in the United States may be able to seek higher payments for its work on a public works project”. Donors listed are contractors using American steel, as their names and reported occupations appear in the campaign finance reports; this does not claim they asked for the bill or for this vote. Gifts are shown with the dates recorded, including any after the vote. The bill became law (Ch. 2024-267).
note.es: Votación en el pleno. El análisis del personal dice que el proyecto beneficia a contratistas que usan acero estadounidense (cita en inglés): “A private contractor that use iron or steel products that are produced in the United States may be able to seek higher payments for its work on a public works project”. Los donantes que aparecen son contratistas que usan acero estadounidense, según sus nombres y ocupaciones en los reportes de campaña; esto no afirma que pidieran el proyecto ni este voto. Las donaciones se muestran con las fechas registradas, incluso las posteriores al voto. El proyecto se convirtió en ley (Ch. 2024-267).
note.ht: Vòt nan sesyon plenyè. Analiz anplwaye a di pwojè a ede kontraktè ki itilize asye ameriken (sitasyon an angle): “A private contractor that use iron or steel products that are produced in the United States may be able to seek higher payments for its work on a public works project”. Donatè ki parèt yo se kontraktè ki itilize asye ameriken, jan non yo ak okipasyon yo parèt nan rapò kanpay yo; sa pa di yo te mande pwojè lwa a ni vòt sa a. Kado yo parèt ak dat yo anrejistre, menm sa ki vini apre vòt la. Pwojè a te tounen lwa (Ch. 2024-267).

note.en: Floor vote: third reading. note.en: Floor vote: third reading. The staff analysis says the bill helps health care practitioners and free clinics: “The bill may have an indeterminate positive fiscal impact on health care practitioners who are able to participate in FRAME or the DSLR Program. The bill may have an indeterminate positive fiscal impact for nonprofit entities that take advantage of the Health Care Screening and Services Grant program”. Donors listed are health care practitioners and free clinics, as their names and reported occupations appear in the campaign finance reports; this does not claim they asked for the bill or for this vote. Gifts are shown with the dates recorded, including any after the vote. The bill became law (Ch. 2024-15).

note.en: Floor vote: passage.
